text: The listed options don't capture the main hazard: using water instead of sterile 0.9% sodium chloride risks hypotonic absorption causing dilutional hyponatraemia, haemolysis, and potentially fatal electrolyte disturbance, plus mucosal irritation and pain. Of the given options, "bladder washout may be unsuccessful" is the closer fit, since water is not the recommended irrigant and the procedure may not achieve its purpose. CONFIDENCE: 55
